entries.english:
Account 1583/84.

Dates: 1583–1584.

Contents: Income from repayments of debts, rents, and the offices (manorial dues, tolls, escorts, etc.); expenditure on debts, interest, messengers' wages, gifts, services, and so forth.

Acquisitions of artistic and craft products:
- Firearms from gunsmiths, including a musketeer from Schorndorf; Erhard Rieger, Peter Zweck, and Georg Rieger, gunsmiths; Hans Kaiser, barrel maker at Suhl; Andreas Rueff and Alexius Beck, gunsmiths; three Stuttgart gunsmiths; Jakob Schlude and Burkhard Kroll, gun-stock makers; and Jakob Stehlin, gunsmith (folios 319r–321v, 372r–373v).
- Crossbows and accessories from Hans Weigenmayer of Nördlingen, including crossbow windlasses (folio 322r).
- Bladed weapons and parts from Adam Baur, blade smith at Urach; Adam Goldschmied; Konrad Schlotterbeck, cutler at Tübingen; and Cyriakus Welsch (folios 320r, 322r, 368v, 373r–v).
- Pole weapons from Georg Hilsenbeck, weaponsmith at Giengen, and Hans Schnee, weaponsmith at Heidenheim (folios 321r–322r).
- Precious-metal cutlery from Abraham Goldschmied (folio 369r).
- Silverware, partly with gemstones, from Georg Bantzer, goldsmith at Augsburg, including gifts for Dr Nikolaus Varnbüler, Dr Anastasius Demler, Dr Johannes Hochmann, Johann Weckerlin, Johann Weron, Wolf Dietrich von Weiler, Melchior Schenk von Rossberg, Hans Konrad Megenzer, Eitel Eck von Reischach, Hermann von Janowitz, Hans Georg von Hallwyl, and Friedrich von Breitenbach; items of unknown origin for the messenger-master, Erasmus von Venningen and his wife, Albrecht von Liebenstein, the Palatine couple of Pfalz-Sulzbach at their child's baptism, Andreas Musmann, and the colonel of Lützelburg; and further silverware from Hans Raiser of Augsburg, Karl Seckler, Abraham Goldschmied, an Augsburg goldsmith, the son of Andreas Türhütter of Nürtingen, and Hans Baumann (folios 328r, 356r–360r, 367r–374r).
- Copperware from Georg Schaich, coppersmith at Stuttgart (folio 311v).
- Jewelry and gemstones from Hans Raiser of Augsburg, including gold ornaments, chains, jewels, necklaces, bracelets, rings, and bridal wreaths for Sophie and her journey to Weimar; a jewel for Maria Christine of the Palatinate, wife of Duke Karl of Sweden; and gemstone rings. Also listed are items of unknown origin, an Augsburg goldsmith, Stefan Schön the gem cutter, Abraham Goldschmied, and Wendel Miller, goldsmith at Augsburg (folios 142r, 317r, 359r, 366r–370r).
- Textiles from Hans Raiser, including Fräulein Sophie's wedding shirt (folio 367r).
- Clocks, some gilded, from the Fugger rent master and Ludwig Mauerbeck (folios 368v, 373r–374r).
- Sculptural figures from Valentin Mohler, citizen of Nuremberg; Sem Schleher of Schwäbisch Hall; Hans Raiser; Abraham Goldschmied; and Georg Bantzer, including portraits of the duke and duchess, epitaphs of Württemberg ancestors, a gilded silver stag, a gold enamelled frog, and stags as New Year's gifts (folios 368r–369v).
- Iron grilles for the epitaphs of Württemberg ancestors in the collegiate church from Martin Rapp, clockmaker at Stuttgart (folio 374r).
- Coins, medals, and metal busts from Valentin Mohler, Karl Seckler, and Abraham Goldschmied (folios 368v–369v).
- Containers from Abraham Goldschmied, including silver boxes, and Hans Distler, locksmith, including an iron chest (folios 369r–374r).
- Furniture from Hans Gräfinger of Regensburg, including two armchairs (folio 374r).
- A wood-and-ivory chess set with silver fittings from Wendel Dietrich, cabinetmaker at Augsburg (folio 373v).
- Repair of a silver writing set by Hans Baumann, goldsmith (folio 373v).
- Fitting of deer antlers by Hans Mayer, crossbow maker (folio 373r).

Extent: 434 leaves.
